Grind
The hook

Every empire starts with one ugly floor.

Rough, cracked concrete goes in. A glossy flake floor comes out. And in-game cash hits your balance.

That before-and-after is the whole game in one hit, and you earn it with your own hands.

Boss

You're the boss

Your name on the van. Your crew. Your floors. Three promises to the player:

01 Build the business

Start your own epoxy flooring outfit from a single garage job.

02 Work like a real pro

Grind, prep, mix, pour, flake. Every stage of the job is hands-on.

03 Get paid

Finish the floor, earn in-game cash, and put it back into the business.

Epoxy

What's in the bucket

This pitch puts DSD's product in every player's hands. The epoxy they mix and pour is Ghostshield Epoxy Max 100.

On the label
Epoxy Max 100
100% solids base coat / Floor coating
  • Hides imperfections
  • Self-leveling
  • Zero VOC

Two containers in the photo. The smaller one is marked B Activator.

Grind
01 Stage 1 of 6

Grind the floor

Open up the concrete.

Steer the grinder across the slab with the on-screen stick and strip the old surface pass by pass. The bar fills as bare concrete shows through.

42%
Clean
02 Stage 2 of 6

Vacuum & clean

No dust left behind.

Run the vacuum over every inch of the ground slab. Watch the grey haze lift and the floor come up clean and ready for coating.

76%
Repair
03 Stage 3 of 6

Repair cracks

Fix what's broken.

Hunt down every crack in the slab and fill it before any coating goes on. Three tools on the belt:

  • Crack filler
  • Patch
  • Trowel
2 / 4
Mix
04 Stage 4 of 6

Mix epoxy

Get the ratio right.

In the bucket: Ghostshield Epoxy Max 100, DSD's product. Pour Part A and Part B, hit the ratio, then run the mixer.

Game screen ratio2A : 1B

Ghostshield's published mixing instructions for Epoxy Max 100: Combine two (2) Part A to one (1) Part B, by volume.

Source: ghostshield.com/product/epoxy-max-100, checked 17 Nov 2026.

Pour
05 Stage 5 of 6

Apply base coat

Lay it down.

Pour the mixed Ghostshield Epoxy Max 100 onto the slab and pull it across. Watch the grey turn to gloss. Choose how you spread it:

  • Squeegee
  • T-bar
  • Roller
60%

On the label  100% solids base coat / Self-leveling / Hides imperfections

Flake
06 Stage 6 of 6

Broadcast flakes

Make it rain.

Pick a flake blend from five on the tray and throw it by hand into the wet coat until the whole floor is covered.

75%

Tap or click anywhere in this deck to throw a handful

Real

Not another beige sim

Cash

How the game earns

Free to download, paid by choice. Proposed model, to be confirmed

01

Rewarded ads

Opt in to watch an ad and boost an in-game job payout or speed up a wait. Never forced mid-job.

02

Style packs

Flake blends, metallic pigments, tool skins and crew gear sold as in-app purchases.

03

Pro pass

04

Brand awareness

Not a sales line, but value for DSD: every player mixes and pours DSD's product, Ghostshield Epoxy Max 100. Proposed Links to DSD coaching online classes inside the game.

Player cash is in-game currency. It is earned on jobs and spent growing the player's business inside the game.

Players buy things. They are never paid real money. Revenue scenarios are on the next two slides.

What if

Revenue scenarios

What in-app purchases could bring in, under three sets of assumptions. Scenario, not a forecast

ConservativeMiddleOptimistic
Players who buy1%Estimate2%Estimate4%Estimate
Average spend per paying player, first 90 days$5.00Estimate$7.26Source 1, Casual$9.80Source 1, Midcore
Store fee15%Sources 2, 315%Sources 2, 315%Sources 2, 3

Estimates, to be adjusted: the share of players who buy in all three cases, and the $5.00 spend. Treating Epoxy Empire as a Casual or Midcore game is also an assumption. Ad revenue is not included.

Source 1: AppsFlyer, The State of App Monetization, 2026 Edition. Average in-app purchase revenue per paying user within 90 days of install: Casual $7.26, Midcore $9.80. For scale on the share who buy, it reports Casino, its highest game category, at 4.95% of installs buying within 30 days. appsflyer.com/resources/reports/app-marketing-monetization-report

Source 2: Apple, App Store Small Business Program. 15% commission for developers with up to 1 million USD in proceeds. developer.apple.com/app-store/small-business-program

Source 3: Google, Play Console Help, Service fees. 10% plus a 5% billing fee on the first $1M (USD) of annual earnings. support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/112622

All three checked 17 Nov 2026.

60

The 60-day build

Four work areas build the game over the next 60 days. Proposed schedule

Days 1 to 15

Graphics development

Screens, menus and art in the mockup's black and gold look.

Days 16 to 30

3D models

Job sites, tools and materials for the six stages.

Days 31 to 45

Game engine physics

How grinding, mixing, spreading and flakes behave in your hands.

Days 46 to 60

Testing

Every job played end to end. Fix, tune, repeat.

In the plan: the four work areas and the 60 days. Proposed  The day ranges and the notes under each area.

Proposed, after the build  Soft launch to tune difficulty, job rewards and retention. Then launch and live: full release, with new floors, systems and tools in regular drops.
